I need to understand how projects load with issues and examine the listOverdueIssues function.

Archived projects lock all attached issues and sub-resources as read-only. Any write operation on an archived issue must throw `AlreadyArchivedError` without modifying state or publishing events. The overdue sweep must ignore issues from archived projects entirely. Reads remain fully functional.

Restoring a project removes all read-only restrictions. Existing permission checks still take precedence over the archive lock.

When an archived issue or comment is targeted, the `AlreadyArchivedError` must name and identify that specific entity rather than switching to the parent project.

The precedence order is now clear. Permission checks run first. Then the system asserts the specific issue or comment is not archived. Finally it checks whether the parent project is archived.

The project archive check must run after the entity's own archive assertion. Otherwise an archived issue inside an archived project would incorrectly report the project as the error source. The same ordering applies to comment creation.
